title: The Rs 2.05 crore question: Can Meta be blamed for what its glasses record?
content: He has alleged he was covertly filmed with Ray-Ban Meta glasses and turned into subject of viral content. His legal notice now raises a larger question: Can Meta be held responsible for designing eyewear that allows unsuspecting bystanders to be recorded?

title: ‘May land me in hot water’: Multan Sultans CEO delivers explosive take on Pak cricket
content: Pakistan Cricket Board's recent squad and coaching changes have drawn significant criticism.  Multan Sultans CEO Gohar Shah voiced concerns over player professionalism and team intensity.  He also highlighted issues within the wider cricket ecosystem, including media and former players.  Shah pointed to bureaucratic hurdles and a lack of incentive for PCB stakeholders.  His assessment offered a candid view on the state of Pakistan cricket.

title: Mark Zuckerberg buys 440-acre Irish castle estate; spokesperson says family is ‘excited’
content: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his spouse Priscilla Chan have acquired the majestic Strancally Castle in County Waterford, Ireland. Spanning around 440 acres, the estate boasts a rich history dating back to 1830. The couple intends to use this beautifully restored property as a retreat during their visits, reinforcing Meta's strong ties to Ireland, where the company has its international headquarters.

title: 'We can resist US unilateralism': Iran president tells Putin on sidelines of SCO summit
content: During a recent dialogue, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian expressed gratitude towards Vladimir Putin for Russia's supportive position. He emphasized the need for Iran and Russia to jointly counter the unilateral actions of the United States. Pezeshkian also condemned the U.S. for its sanctions and breaches of international law. Putin, in response, endorsed the memorandum aimed at fostering cooperation between Iran and Russia amidst escalating tensions with the U.S.

title: NEET protest FIRs quashed: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke calls SC move ‘absolute justice’
content: The Supreme Court's recent verdict has annulled all FIRs filed against students engaged in protests related to NEET across the country. This notable decision serves justice to the protesting individuals and their grieving families. Moreover, it mandates the government to offer compensation to the relatives of those who tragically took their own lives. CJP's Abhijeet Dipke heralded this ruling as essential justice for all participants.

title: Bumrah, Samson back; Pandya misses out as India announce squad for Afghanistan T20Is
content: The Indian cricket team has officially unveiled their 15-member squad for the T20I series against Afghanistan, with Shreyas Iyer as captain and Tilak Varma as vice-captain. The pace attack is bolstered by the return of Jasprit Bumrah, alongside Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana. Notable batsmen include Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan, although some players still await fitness clearance prior to the series start.

title: Musk's $60B purchase of Cursor that made Sam Altman 'upset' has an 'indian connection'
content: Elon Musk's SpaceX recently acquired the AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion.  This significant deal has brought co-founder Aman Sanger and his Indian family roots into focus.  Sanger, an MIT graduate, co-founded Cursor in 2022, which quickly achieved substantial growth.  The acquisition reportedly granted its founders billions in SpaceX shares.  This event also adds a new dimension to Musk's rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

title: Heavy rain causes cave-in on Ganga Expressway ramp, carpet used as quick fix
content: A Ganga Expressway ramp in Unnao experienced a cave-in after heavy rainfall on Tuesday. Workers temporarily covered the damaged section to divert gushing rainwater effectively. The concessionaire and contractor swiftly repaired the affected portion within two and a half hours. Continuous rain also caused waterlogging at the nearby toll plaza on the expressway. Long-term measures are planned to prevent future waterlogging issues at the toll booths.

title: Closed for decades, Pittsburgh's 102-foot lookout is being restored for $3m
content: The historic North Park Observation Tower in Pittsburgh is poised to reopen its doors after being closed for years. A comprehensive restoration effort is underway, focusing on the beloved 1937 building and its staircase, while also enhancing the surrounding park area with fresh landscaping and improved accessibility. Funded by a mix of public and private investments, the landmark is anticipated to welcome guests once more by 2027.

title: Meet Jasmyn Blackburn, the kindergarten teacher making dopamine dressing a hit
content: Jasmyn Blackburn, a kindergarten teacher, uses colorful and sparkly clothing to inspire her young students.  She believes in 'dopamine dressing,' which means wearing clothes that bring happiness.  Her unique style has gained a significant following on social media platforms.  Blackburn's wardrobe features many school-themed items, reflecting her passion for teaching.  She encourages others to find joy in their personal style and express themselves.

title: OpenAI to Apple: This dispute is your mess, and you are blaming everyone
content: OpenAI has pushed back against Apple's claims of trade secret theft in a recent federal court document. OpenAI asserts that internal strife at Apple is to blame for the current legal confrontation, while Apple alleges that its former staff members improperly extracted proprietary data upon leaving for OpenAI. OpenAI maintains that employees are entitled to seek new professional ventures, spotlighting a legal dispute that traces back to their earlier collaboration.

title: India’s tech jobs face another jolt: Oracle to cut 3,000, Microsoft puts 500 on PIPs
content: Global tech giant Microsoft has put around 500 employees in India on performance improvement plans (PIPs), while Oracle is preparing to cut roughly 3,000 jobs in the country as technology companies reorganise their workforces and redirect spending towards newer areas.

title: Fish video row: Ajay Rai files defamation case against CM Yogi for 'hurting faith'

The controversy began after a video of fish preparation at a Congress event surfaced. Adityanath had accused Rai of duplicity for attending the event. Rai denied eating fish and challenged the chief minister to provide proof.

title: ‘Most shocking decision ever’: Shahid Afridi blasts Pakistan’s Test shake-up

title: Shane Bieber’s wife Kara Maxine’s pregnancy style: What does her life look like?

title: Dragged 60ft under a bus, now fighting for UFC contract: How did Liam McCracken survive?

Doctors feared his injuries would prevent him from fighting professionally again.  Remarkably, McCracken recovered and returned to fighting after nearly two years. title: 'He killed her, then went back to sleep': Calm of Hyderabad nurse's killer baffles cops

The accused returned to his garage and slept after committing the crime.  Mobile data and forensic evidence helped investigators crack the difficult case.  Police are checking the accused's criminal record in Bihar.

title: Bird species rose from 29 to 37 after Colorado couple restored family ranch
content: Lance and Lisa Wheeler's Colorado ranch has transformed into a sanctuary for grassland birds, boasting a remarkable doubling in species detection since 2019. Their innovative farming methods, coupled with adaptive grazing strategies, promote rich habitats that support diverse wildlife. As evidenced by a 26% increase on the ranch's Bird-Friendliness Index, this holistic approach successfully merges livestock management with conservation efforts.

title: Should Novak Djokovic take a leaf from Lionel Messi and retire?
content: Now, Messi and Djokovic do have a lot in common. Both came from impoverished backgrounds and became the greatest ever to play their respective sports. Both were even born in the same year, just 33 days apart. Both chased dreams that seemed unattainable, with families who bet their futures on their children’s success. Both had similarly close paternal relationships and left home early to train. In their early days, both even faced similar physical limitations. Messi needed growth hormones; Djokovic switched his diet and conditioning to produce extraordinary endurance hitherto unseen in tennis.

title: Union minister Chirag Paswan gets death threat; seeks protection

His office has formally communicated this serious threat to the Union home secretary.  The contents and delivery circumstances will undergo a thorough security assessment.  Further details regarding the threat and security measures remain unavailable.

title: Watch: Woman with mental health history charges at NYPD officers with kitchen knives

title: Pakistan cricket in chaos: Misbah resigns as PCB selector amid Test squad shake-up

After facing backlash from recent losses to England, several players and coaches have been dismissed, paving the way for five uncapped players to join the Test squad. Misbah's exit further complicates the current challenges within Pakistan cricket.

Road levelling work is underway, and repairs will be completed soon.

title: Former UK PM Keir Starmer to step down as MP: Report

title: India's GDP grows 7.8% in Q1: Factors powering the economy despite global turmoil

Additionally, investment activity picked up pace, enhancing the overall economic landscape. This achievement stands out amid global geopolitical tensions and market fluctuations, reinforcing India's status as the fastest-growing major economy in the world.

title: Bending ultrathin diamond sheets generates electricity, study finds
content: Researchers have identified a piezoelectric effect in ultrathin diamond membranes.  This effect, previously unseen in bulk diamond, appears in thin polycrystalline sheets.  Grain boundaries within these membranes are responsible for generating electrical responses when deformed.  The strongest piezoelectric response was observed in membranes approximately five micrometres thick.  This discovery opens doors for new applications in energy harvesting and smart electronics.

title: OBC creamy layer: SC agrees to hear Centre's plea against income-only criteria
content:
SC agrees to hear Centre's plea on OBC creamy layer ruling

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear the Centre's plea challenging the retrospective application of its ruling that parents' income cannot be the sole criterion for determining the creamy layer among Other Backward Classes (OBC) candidates. Also read: Govt seeks 2 years to frame creamy layer criteria for PSU, private staff kids The ruling had held that the status and category of a parent's job must also be considered, along with the Income/Wealth Test, while determining whether a candidate should be excluded from OBC reservation. The matter concerns the criteria used to determine the creamy layer, which identifies relatively advanced sections among OBCs who are excluded from the benefits of reservation. More details awaited.

End of Article
